experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while waiting for the show.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal pool rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, a silica mud mask ritual, and a swim-up bar serving Icelandic craft beer. The surreal lava field backdrop makes it a bucket-list hot spring experience.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Morning (to avoid crowds) or Evening (for northern lights potential in season)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and steaming vents. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a glimpse into traditional Icelandic bathing culture in a stunning rural setting.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and cultural landmarks on a guided walking tour. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, and Icelandic hot dogs. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church, the colorful old harbor, and local artisan shops.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's breathtaking rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a natural geothermal hot spring soak at the end. The hike winds through obsidian lava fields, steaming fumaroles, and vivid mineral-streaked hillsides — one of Iceland's most dramatic landscapes.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and pick up a pre-booked budget rental car (essential for Iceland travel). Stop at Bonus supermarket near Reykjavík on the way to stock up on groceries for the trip — this is one of the biggest money-saving tips in Iceland. Drive approximately 1.5–2 hours to your accommodation in the Golden Circle & Þingvellir area.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your boutique stay in the Golden Circle area. If skies are clear, step outside after dark (around 17:00–18:00 sunset in January) and scan the sky for the Northern Lights — your accommodation area has low light pollution making it ideal. Check aurora forecast apps like Vedur.is (Iceland Met Office) for real-time alerts.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport (budget ~1,500 ISK / ~$11 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from airport or grab a quick bite at a Reykjavík Bonus or Krónan supermarket during your grocery stop (budget ~800–1,200 ISK)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at your accommodation using groceries purchased en route — pasta, canned soup, or local skyr with bread (budget ~1,000–1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January days in Iceland are very short — only about 5–6 hours of daylight. Temperatures average -1°C to 4°C. Roads can be icy; drive carefully and check road conditions at road.is. Aurora activity is highest between 22:00–02:00.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and free to enter (parking fee ~750 ISK). Walk the Almannagjá Gorge, which sits on the rift between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Explore the historic Lögberg (Law Rock) and the crystal-clear Öxará River. Dress in layers — January temperatures here can feel biting with wind chill.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the famous Geysir Geothermal Area (free entry). Watch the Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting water 15–40 meters into the air. Explore the surrounding hot spring fields and bubbling mud pools. Nearby, visit Gullfoss Waterfall (free entry) — one of Iceland's most iconic two-tiered waterfalls, dramatic in winter with possible ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation. Check aurora forecast — if KP index is above 3 and skies are clear, drive to a dark spot near Þingvellir lake for Northern Lights viewing. Bring thermos with hot chocolate or tea.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — oatmeal, skyr, toast with Icelandic butter (budget ~500–700 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade sandwich and snacks from your grocery haul to eat at Geysir or Gullfoss (budget ~0 extra cost)
meals.dinner: Cook at accommodation — try making Kjötsúpa (Icelandic lamb soup) with pre-bought ingredients from Bonus (budget ~1,200–1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle route (Þingvellir → Geysir → Gullfoss) is approximately 230 km round trip from the Golden Circle area. Gullfoss can be slippery in winter — wear ice cleats/microspikes if available. Parking fees at Geysir ~750 ISK.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Kerið Volcanic Crater (entry fee ~400 ISK — one of Iceland's cheapest paid attractions). Walk the rim of this striking red and black volcanic caldera with a turquoise lake at the bottom. The contrast of colors against winter snow is stunning. Takes about 45–60 minutes to explore fully.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — one of Iceland's oldest and most affordable natural hot springs (entry ~3,000–3,500 ISK vs. Blue Lagoon's ~8,000–10,000+ ISK). Soak in the geothermally heated pool surrounded by steaming vents and a small geyser. This is a quintessential Icelandic hot spring experience without the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to accommodation. Stop at the small town of Selfoss on the way if needed for additional supplies at Krónan supermarket. Aurora watch from accommodation grounds — January offers long dark nights ideal for sightings.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — scrambled eggs, Icelandic rye bread (Rúgbrauð), and skyr (budget ~600 ISK)
meals.lunch: Bring packed lunch to Secret Lagoon or eat at their small café (soup of the day ~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Cook at accommodation — grilled Icelandic lamb chops or fish with potatoes and vegetables from grocery store (budget ~1,500–2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon is located about 20–30 minutes from the Golden Circle hub. Book in advance online as capacity can be limited. Bring your own towel to avoid rental fees (~500 ISK). Swimsuit is required.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip toward the South Coast. Drive to Seljalandsfoss Waterfall (parking fee ~750 ISK) — in summer you can walk behind it, but in winter the path behind may be closed due to ice. Still spectacular to view from the front with winter ice formations. Then drive 10 minutes to Skógafoss Waterfall (free to view from base) — a majestic 60-meter wide waterfall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach near Vík (free entry). Walk along the dramatic black volcanic sand beach, see the towering Reynisdrangar basalt sea stacks, and explore the Hálsanef basalt column cave. WARNING: Never turn your back to the ocean — sneaker waves are extremely dangerous here. Then drive into the small village of Vík for a quick look around.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the Golden Circle area (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Stop for a budget dinner in Selfoss or Hveragerði. Aurora check before bed.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before early departure (budget ~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from home — eat at Skógafoss or Reynisfjara beach parking area (budget ~0)
meals.dinner: Kaffi Krús in Hveragerði or Gamla Fjósið restaurant — look for daily specials (budget ~2,500–3,500 ISK). Alternatively, cook at home for ~1,200 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast day trip is approximately 300–350 km round trip. Start early to maximize the limited daylight hours (roughly 10:00–15:30 usable light in January). Roads on the South Coast are generally well-maintained but check road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at accommodation. Use the morning to review aurora forecasts, plan upcoming days, and do laundry if facilities are available. Alternatively, take a short walk around Þingvellir lake area near accommodation — beautiful and free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hveragerði — Iceland's 'Hot Spring Town' (about 30–40 minutes from Golden Circle hub). Walk the geothermal park in town center (small entry fee ~500–800 ISK or free to walk around). The town sits on extremely active geothermal ground with steaming vents everywhere. Visit the local greenhouse cooperative where tomatoes and bananas are grown using geothermal energy.
day_by_day.evening: Hike the Reykjadalur Hot Spring Thermal River trail from Hveragerði — a 3 km (each way) hike through a geothermal valley to a naturally heated river where you can bathe for FREE. Bring swimsuit, towel, and a headlamp as it will be dark. The hike takes about 45–60 minutes each way. This is one of Iceland's best free hot spring experiences.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed self-catered breakfast — pancakes with skyr and berries (budget ~600–800 ISK)
meals.lunch: Grab a hot dog at Hveragerði — Icelandic hot dogs (pylsur) are a beloved budget food at ~500–700 ISK each
meals.dinner: Self-catered warm meal at accommodation after the hike — hearty soup or stew from slow cooker if available (budget ~1,000–1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hike in January requires proper winter gear — waterproof boots, layers, headlamp, and a dry bag for clothes. The trail can be icy. Changing facilities are basic (small wooden screens). The hot river is genuinely warm and magical under the stars. Arrive by 15:00 to hike in remaining daylight and hike back in the dark with headlamp.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Reykjavík (approximately 45–60 minutes from the Golden Circle area). Explore the city on foot — visit Hallgrímskirkja Church (exterior is free; tower entry ~1,000 ISK for panoramic views). Walk Skólavörðustígur street lined with colorful shops and cafés. Visit the Sun Voyager sculpture by the waterfront — free and iconic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Reykjavík: Walk along the Tjörnin Pond (free), visit the Harpa Concert Hall exterior (free), and stroll through the old harbor area. Visit the Reykjavík Flea Market (Kolaportið) if it's a weekend — great for cheap local snacks like Hákarl (fermented shark) and Hangikjöt (smoked lamb). Browse the colorful streets of the 101 Reykjavík district.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavík's budget-friendly food scene before driving back. Check aurora forecast — the drive back through rural areas offers excellent viewing opportunities if lights appear.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before leaving accommodation (budget ~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — Reykjavík's most famous hot dog stand near the harbor, ~500–700 ISK per hot dog. A true Icelandic institution.
meals.dinner: Hlöllabátar (Icelandic sub sandwiches) or Noodle Station (Thai-style noodle soup ~1,800–2,200 ISK) — both are popular budget options in Reykjavík

day_by_day.notes: Parking in Reykjavík can be expensive (Zone 1 ~250 ISK/hour). Park in the outer zones or near BSÍ bus terminal for cheaper rates. Many Reykjavík museums are free on specific days — check schedules. The city is very walkable once parked.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the Snæfellsnes Peninsula direction OR explore more of the Golden Circle area — visit Laugarvatn Fontana Geothermal Baths (entry ~3,500–4,500 ISK) on the shores of Lake Laugarvatn. This smaller geothermal spa has natural steam saunas built directly over hot springs and a beautiful lake setting. Much more affordable and authentic than the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Laugarvatn village and walk along the lake shore. Drive to Háifoss Waterfall (one of Iceland's tallest at 122 meters) if roads permit in winter — check road.is as the F-road (F225) may be closed. If closed, alternatively visit Hjálparfoss (accessible year-round, free) — a beautiful double waterfall in the Þjórsá river area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation. Dedicated aurora hunting night — drive to the darkest spot you can find near Þingvellir lake, turn off car lights, and wait. Bring sleeping bags to stay warm in the car while watching. Set aurora alerts on Vedur.is app.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — Icelandic oatmeal with brown sugar and raisins (budget ~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Café at Laugarvatn Fontana serves fresh rye bread baked underground in geothermal sand — try the geothermal bread with Icelandic butter (~1,200–1,500 ISK). A unique experience.
meals.dinner: Self-catered hearty dinner — Icelandic fish stew (Plokkfiskur) made from scratch with cod and potatoes from Bonus (budget ~1,200–1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Laugarvatn Fontana is a highlight — the geothermal steam sauna experience is unique to Iceland. Bring your own towel. January KP index forecasts are crucial — KP3 or above with clear skies gives excellent aurora chances in the Þingvellir area.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning drive to explore the Langjökull Glacier area viewpoints (accessible viewpoints from the road are free). Drive Route 52 toward Húsafell — the mountain scenery in winter is dramatic. Stop at Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls near Húsafell (free entry, parking ~750 ISK) — Hraunfossar is extraordinary, with water seeping through lava fields for hundreds of meters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Deildartunguhver — Europe's most powerful hot spring (free to view). Located near Reykholt, it produces 180 liters of 100°C water per second. The steam and boiling water are mesmerizing in cold winter air. Visit Snorrastofa cultural center in Reykholt (small entry fee ~1,000 ISK) dedicated to medieval Norse poet Snorri Sturluson.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Golden Circle accommodation (approximately 1.5 hours). Stop at a supermarket if needed. Aurora watch from accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early departure breakfast — rye bread with smoked salmon and cream cheese (budget ~700 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from home — eat at Hraunfossar parking area (budget ~0 extra)
meals.dinner: Self-catered — grilled Icelandic lamb burger with homemade fries (budget ~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: This is a longer driving day (~250–300 km round trip). Route 52 (Kaldidalur) may be closed in winter — check road.is. If closed, take Route 1 via Borgarnes as an alternative. Hraunfossar in winter with snow and ice is absolutely stunning and often uncrowded.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated relaxation and hot spring morning. Visit Gamla Laugin (Secret Lagoon) again OR try the Laugar Spa in Laugarvatn for a different experience. Alternatively, if budget is tight, hike back to Reykjadalur Hot Spring River (free) for another soak — the experience is different each time depending on weather and light conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the area around Flúðir village — small, authentic Icelandic farming community. Visit the local greenhouse cooperative where exotic plants are grown using geothermal energy (small tour possible). Drive around the Hvítá River area and look for Icelandic horses in the fields — they are everywhere in this region and love human interaction through fences.
day_by_day.evening: Photography evening — the Golden Circle area is excellent for night photography. Set up near Þingvellir lake or Geysir for long-exposure shots of the night sky and potential aurora. Many photography spots are free and accessible. Connect with other travelers at accommodation for aurora-spotting tips.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — skyr parfait with granola and Icelandic blueberries (budget ~600 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and a thermos of soup for the afternoon exploration (budget ~300–500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner at Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn (fish of the day ~3,500–4,500 ISK) — one budget splurge for the trip. Alternatively cook at home for ~1,200 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Day 9 is intentionally lighter to allow for rest and flexibility. January travel in Iceland can be physically demanding — cold, icy roads, and late nights aurora hunting take a toll. Use this day to recharge. Check weather forecast for the remaining days and adjust plans accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Westman Islands (Vestmannaeyjar) ferry terminal at Landeyjahöfn (approximately 1 hour from Golden Circle area). Take the Herjólfur ferry to Heimaey Island (ferry ~2,800–3,500 ISK each way). The 35-minute crossing offers views of dramatic sea cliffs. Arrive on Heimaey and explore the town and harbor area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Heimaey Island: Visit the Eldheimar Museum (entry ~2,500 ISK) — a fascinating museum built around a house buried in the 1973 Eldfell volcanic eruption. Hike up Eldfell volcano (free) for panoramic views of the island, ocean, and mainland Iceland. The volcanic soil is still warm underfoot in places.
day_by_day.evening: Take the return ferry to Landeyjahöfn and drive back to accommodation. This is a full but rewarding day trip. Check ferry schedules in advance as winter sailings may be reduced.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before early departure (budget ~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Einsi Kaldi or Slippurinn restaurant on Heimaey (Slippurinn is famous but pricey — budget alternative is the local bakery/café in town for soup and bread ~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation — simple pasta with Icelandic meat sauce (budget ~1,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules at herjolfur.is well in advance — winter schedules are reduced and can be cancelled due to weather. The Westman Islands are a unique and often-overlooked destination. Heimaey is the only inhabited island and has a surprisingly vibrant small-town culture. Total cost for day including ferry: ~7,000–8,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Þingvellir National Park for a different experience — explore the Silfra Fissure area (the fissure itself is free to view; snorkeling/diving requires a tour at ~15,000–20,000 ISK which is not budget-friendly but can be considered a splurge). Walk the Lögberg trail and Hakið viewpoint trail (free) for stunning views over the rift valley and Lake Þingvallavatn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Nesjavellir Geothermal Power Plant (free to view from outside and nearby viewpoints) — one of Iceland's largest geothermal plants with massive steam columns visible from a distance. The landscape here is otherworldly. Continue to the Þingvallavatn lake shore for a peaceful winter walk — the lake is Iceland's largest natural lake.
day_by_day.evening: Final serious aurora hunting night. Check Vedur.is for the best forecast window. Drive to a pre-scouted dark location (Þingvellir lake north shore is excellent). Bring all warm gear, thermos, snacks, and camera equipment. Stay out as long as conditions allow — this may be your last best chance.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — French toast with Icelandic butter and jam (budget ~600 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack a hot thermos of soup and sandwiches for the Þingvellir exploration (budget ~400 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered — traditional Icelandic lamb stew with root vegetables (budget ~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January 25th statistically offers good aurora chances if solar activity cooperates. The KP index forecast 3–4 days out becomes more reliable — plan your best aurora night based on the most current forecast. Þingvellir's protected dark sky status makes it one of the best aurora viewing locations in Southwest Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — revisit your favorite spot from the trip or explore somewhere you missed. Suggested: Drive the Öxnadalur valley area or revisit Gullfoss in different light conditions. Alternatively, visit the Geothermal Exhibition at Hellisheiðarvirkjun Power Plant on Route 1 near Reykjavík (entry ~1,500–2,000 ISK) — educational and fascinating.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavík for final souvenir shopping on a budget. Best budget souvenirs: Icelandic wool products from Kolaportið flea market, local chocolate from Nói Síríus brand at supermarkets, Brennivín miniatures, and Icelandic sea salt. Avoid tourist trap shops on Laugavegur for better prices at local stores and supermarkets.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Reykjavík. Splurge slightly on a memorable meal. Explore the harbor area one last time. If aurora forecast is good, drive out of Reykjavík city lights for one final viewing attempt. Pack bags and prepare for early departure.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — use up remaining groceries (budget ~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Reykjavík food hall or Grái Kötturinn café (budget-friendly brunch spot, ~1,800–2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Sægreifinn (Sea Baron) — famous lobster soup in Reykjavík harbor, ~1,500–2,000 ISK per bowl. One of the best value meals in Iceland.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to fill up the rental car with fuel (fuel is expensive in Iceland — budget ~5,000–8,000 ISK for a full tank depending on car size). Return rental car with a full tank to avoid surcharges. Check rental car for any damage before returning. Settle any outstanding accommodation payments.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of accommodation. Drive to Keflavík International Airport (approximately 1–1.5 hours from Golden Circle area). Allow extra time for winter road conditions. Return rental car at the airport — most rental companies are in the airport complex or a short shuttle away.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in for departure flight. Explore the duty-free shop at Keflavík Airport — Icelandic spirits (Brennivín), chocolates, and wool products are often cheaper duty-free than in town. Enjoy a final Icelandic hot dog or skyr at the airport café.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with incredible memories of the Northern Lights, geothermal hot springs, dramatic winter landscapes, and the unique Icelandic culture.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered final breakfast at accommodation or grab something at a petrol station on the way to the airport (budget ~800–1,200 ISK)
meals.lunch: Airport café or bring remaining snacks from accommodation (budget ~1,500–2,000 ISK at airport)
meals.dinner: On the flight or at destination airport

day_by_day.notes: BUDGET SUMMARY ESTIMATE (per person, 13 days): Accommodation (pre-booked) — variable; Groceries & self-catered meals ~25,000–30,000 ISK; Eating out (selective) ~15,000–20,000 ISK; Fuel for rental car ~15,000–20,000 ISK; Entry fees & activities ~20,000–25,000 ISK; Miscellaneous ~5,000 ISK. TOTAL estimated spend (excluding flights & rental car base cost): ~80,000–100,000 ISK (~$580–$730 USD) for 13 days. Key savings: cooking most meals, using free natural attractions, avoiding Blue Lagoon, and choosing Secret Lagoon and free hot springs instead.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while waiting for the show.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and pick up pre-booked rental car (4WD recommended for January conditions).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Keflavík toward the Golden Circle area (~1.5 hrs). Stop at the iconic Hellisheiði Geothermal Power Plant visitor center en route for a fascinating introduction to Iceland's renewable energy and geothermal landscape. Arrive and check in to your boutique stay in the Golden Circle & Þingvellir area.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your accommodation, freshen up, and take a short evening walk around the property to acclimate to Iceland's winter darkness. Keep an eye on the northern lights forecast app (Vedur.is) — if aurora activity is rated 3+ and skies are clear, step outside for your first potential northern lights sighting right from the accommodation grounds.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a bite at Keflavík Airport (Fljúgur Café offers sandwiches and soups at mid-range prices)
meals.lunch: Pick up supplies at a Krónan or Bónus supermarket en route for a self-catered light lunch in the car or at the guesthouse
meals.dinner: Dinner at your boutique guesthouse restaurant or a nearby local spot such as Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn (~20 min drive) — known for fresh Icelandic lamb and fish dishes, mains around 3,500–5,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: January days are very short (~5 hours of daylight, roughly 11:00–16:00). Road conditions can be icy — drive carefully and check road.is before every journey. Download the 112 Iceland safety app.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Þingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the meeting point of the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Walk the Almannagjá gorge rift valley trail (easy, ~2 km) and visit the historic Alþingi parliament site. Arrive by 10:30 to make the most of limited daylight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Geysir Geothermal Area (~45 min from Þingvellir). Watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting water 20–30 meters into the air. Explore the surrounding hot spring pools and fumaroles. Visit the Geysir Center for warming up and browsing the exhibition.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — join the small-group guided jeep tour departing from the Golden Circle area. Your guide will drive away from light pollution using real-time aurora forecasts to find the best viewing spots. Tours typically run 21:00–00:00.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at your boutique guesthouse (included or ~1,500–2,000 ISK) — skyr, rye bread, smoked salmon, eggs
meals.lunch: Café at the Geysir Center — lamb soup (kjötsúpa) and fresh bread, budget ~2,000–3,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Gullfoss Kaffi near Gullfoss waterfall or Hotel Geysir restaurant — hearty Icelandic fish stew or pan-fried Arctic char, mains ~3,500–5,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Book the Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep in advance — January is peak aurora season but tours fill up quickly. Dress in thermal base layers, mid-layers, and a waterproof outer shell. Hand warmers are recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Gullfoss Waterfall (~10 min from Geysir area), one of Iceland's most powerful waterfalls. In January the falls are often partially frozen and dramatically lit. Walk the viewing platforms and take in the ice-encrusted canyon. Allow 1–1.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Laugarvatn Fontana Geothermal Baths on the shores of Lake Laugarvatn (~30 min drive). Soak in naturally heated mineral pools, use the steam rooms built directly over geothermal vents, and try the traditional geothermal rye bread baked underground. A perfect mid-range hot spring experience (~4,200 ISK entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to your guesthouse. Check aurora forecast — if conditions are favorable (clear skies, KP index 3+), drive to a dark spot away from any settlement for independent northern lights viewing. Þingvellir lake area offers excellent dark skies.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — skyr with berries, oatmeal, Icelandic pancakes
meals.lunch: Laugarvatn Fontana Café — try the famous geothermal rye bread with Icelandic butter and smoked trout (~1,500–2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Lindin Restaurant, Laugarvatn — award-winning New Nordic cuisine using local ingredients; Arctic char, lamb, and seasonal vegetables. Two courses ~6,000–8,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Laugarvatn Fontana is one of Iceland's most authentic geothermal bath experiences. Bring a swimsuit and towel (rental available on-site). The lake dip in January is for the brave — water around 5°C!

day_by_day.morning: Drive south toward the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir (~45 min from Golden Circle hub). This is Iceland's oldest swimming pool, dating to 1891, set in a geothermal field with small geysers and hot springs bubbling nearby. Soak in the 38–40°C naturally heated outdoor pool surrounded by steam and possibly snow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Flúðir and its surrounding mushroom farms and greenhouse tomato/cucumber operations (a quirky Icelandic winter agriculture story). Drive back through the Golden Circle and stop at Kerið Volcanic Crater Lake (~30 min from Flúðir) — a striking red and black caldera with a turquoise lake. Entry fee ~400 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Relax evening at the guesthouse. Review photos, plan upcoming days, and enjoy a quiet night in. If aurora forecast is strong, wrap up and head outside for sky watching.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast
meals.lunch: Pack a self-catered lunch from guesthouse or supermarket supplies — rye bread sandwiches with skyr and fruit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Árnes Guesthouse restaurant or self-catered dinner at accommodation using local ingredients purchased from Krónan — Icelandic lamb chops with roasted root vegetables (~2,500 ISK for groceries)

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is smaller and more affordable than the Blue Lagoon (~3,000 ISK entry) and offers a more authentic, less touristy experience. Arrive early to avoid the midday crowd.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip toward South Iceland — drive the Ring Road east toward Seljalandsfoss waterfall (~1.5 hrs from Golden Circle). Walk behind the curtain of water (icy in January — crampons available for rent nearby). Continue 10 min to Skógafoss waterfall for dramatic rainbow-in-mist photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Sólheimajökull glacier (~30 min from Skógafoss) for a self-guided walk to the glacier tongue viewpoint, or join a short guided glacier walk if pre-booked (~12,000 ISK). The black sand and ice landscape is otherworldly in winter light.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Golden Circle area (~1.5 hrs). Stop at Hvolsvöllur for dinner before the final stretch. Check northern lights forecast for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Early guesthouse breakfast to maximize daylight hours
meals.lunch: Skógar Museum Café near Skógafoss — lamb soup and Icelandic pastries, ~2,000–3,000 ISK
meals.dinner: The Lava Restaurant at Hotel Rangá or Eldstó Art Café in Hvolsvöllur — hearty lamb burger or fish and chips, ~3,500–5,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: January roads to South Iceland can be challenging. Check road.is before departing. Seljalandsfoss path behind the waterfall may be closed due to ice — always follow safety signs. Sunrise is around 11:15, sunset around 15:45 in January.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Þingvellir National Park more deeply — take the Öxará River walk and visit the historic Drowning Pool (Drekkingarhylur) and the Law Rock (Lögberg). In winter the park is beautifully quiet and often dusted with snow. Allow 2–3 hours for a leisurely exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Nesjavellir Geothermal Power Station (~20 min from Þingvellir) for an exterior view of Iceland's second-largest geothermal plant steaming dramatically against the mountain backdrop. Continue to Þingvallavatn lake shore for a winter walk and birdwatching (whooper swans often present in winter).
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep (second booking if available, or alternative independent hunt). Þingvellir's dark skies make it one of the best areas in southwest Iceland for aurora viewing. If skipping the tour, drive to Þingvellir's parking areas after dark with a thermos of hot chocolate.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast
meals.lunch: Þingvellir National Park Visitor Center Café — open in winter with soups and light meals, ~2,000–2,500 ISK
meals.dinner: ION Adventure Hotel restaurant (~15 min from Þingvellir) — upscale but accessible New Nordic tasting menu; budget ~8,000–12,000 ISK for a special dinner splurge, or opt for their bar menu at ~4,000–6,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: ION Hotel is architecturally stunning and positioned perfectly for northern lights viewing from its glass-walled restaurant. Even if not staying there, dining is a worthwhile splurge experience.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in, enjoy a leisurely guesthouse breakfast, and review the week's highlights. Use the morning to do laundry if needed, restock groceries, and plan the second half of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Haukadalur Valley geothermal area for a self-guided walk among mud pools, fumaroles, and hot spring terraces beyond the main Geysir tourist area. This quieter section rewards curious explorers. Alternatively, visit the nearby Skálholt Cathedral, Iceland's most historically significant religious site, with a small museum.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed dinner and early evening stargazing/aurora watch from the guesthouse garden or nearby field. January often brings the clearest aurora nights of the year when weather cooperates.

meals.breakfast: Extended guesthouse breakfast — take your time
meals.lunch: Self-catered lunch at the guesthouse — assemble Icelandic open-faced sandwiches (smørrebrød style) with smoked salmon, pickled herring, and skyr
meals.dinner: Guesthouse dinner or local restaurant — try traditional Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa) and skyr cake for dessert, ~3,000–4,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day is important for a 13-day journey. Use this day to recharge physically and mentally. Check weather forecasts for the upcoming week and adjust plans accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Reykjavik (~45 min from Golden Circle hub) for a city day. Start with a visit to Hallgrímskirkja Church — take the elevator to the tower for panoramic views over the colorful city rooftops and harbor. Explore the surrounding Skólavörðustígur street with its art galleries and craft shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Harpa Concert Hall on the harbor — the geometric glass facade is spectacular. Walk the old harbor area and visit the Sun Voyager sculpture. Explore the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn) for an excellent overview of Icelandic history and culture (~2,000 ISK entry).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Reykjavik before driving back to the Golden Circle. Explore the lively 101 Reykjavik restaurant scene. Return to guesthouse by 21:00–22:00.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast before departing
meals.lunch: Café Babalú or Bergsson Mathús in Reykjavik — soups, sandwiches, and excellent coffee in cozy settings, ~2,500–3,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Sægreifinn (Sea Baron) on the harbor — famous lobster soup and grilled fish on skewers, excellent mid-range value at ~3,000–4,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Reykjavik is compact and very walkable. Wear good waterproof footwear as streets can be icy. Most museums and attractions accept card payment. The city is safe and easy to navigate independently.

day_by_day.morning: Snowmobile or snowshoeing experience — book a guided snowshoe tour through the Þingvellir lava fields and birch forests (several operators offer half-day tours from ~12,000 ISK). Alternatively, rent snowshoes independently and explore marked trails around the national park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Þingvellir Information Center for an in-depth exhibition about the geological and historical significance of the site. Walk the Hakið viewpoint trail for sweeping views over the rift valley and Þingvallavatn lake — the largest natural lake in Iceland.
day_by_day.evening: Aurora hunting evening — drive to the northern shore of Þingvallavatn lake, away from all light sources. Set up on the lakeshore for reflections of the northern lights in the still water (one of Iceland's most magical photography opportunities when conditions align).

meals.breakfast: Early guesthouse breakfast
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from guesthouse — hot soup in a thermos, sandwiches, and Icelandic chocolate (Nói Síríus brand)
meals.dinner: Guesthouse dinner or nearby local restaurant — baked cod with Icelandic potatoes and butter sauce, ~3,500–5,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: For the best northern lights lake reflection shots, bring a tripod. Even smartphone cameras can capture aurora with night mode if you use a stable surface. Check the Vedur.is aurora forecast at 18:00 for the evening prediction.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Hveragerði Hot Spring Town (~40 min south of Golden Circle). This small town sits directly on geothermal ground — hot water bubbles up in gardens and greenhouses throughout. Visit the EARTH Geothermal Park in the town center for a fascinating walk among hot springs, mud pools, and steaming vents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Reykjadalur Hot Spring River Trail from Hveragerði — a 6 km round-trip hike (~2.5 hrs) up a geothermal valley to a naturally heated river where you can bathe in 38–40°C flowing hot spring water. In January this hike is done partly in darkness — bring headlamps. The snow-covered landscape is stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Return to guesthouse, warm up, and enjoy a relaxed evening. The Reykjadalur hike is physically demanding — rest and recover. Light aurora watch from the guesthouse.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast
meals.lunch: Varma Restaurant or a local café in Hveragerði — greenhouse tomato soup (grown geothermally) and fresh bread, ~2,000–3,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered hearty dinner at guesthouse — Icelandic lamb stew cooked in the kitchenette if available, or guesthouse restaurant

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hike is one of Iceland's most unique experiences — bathing in a hot river in a snow-covered valley. Bring a dry bag for clothes, a swimsuit, flip-flops for changing, and a headlamp for the January darkness. The trail is well-marked but can be slippery.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula for a day trip (~2 hrs from Golden Circle). Visit the dramatic Kirkjufell mountain (Iceland's most photographed mountain) near Grundarfjörður — the iconic arrow-shaped peak with the Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall in the foreground is spectacular in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Snæfellsnes coast to Snæfellsjökull National Park — the glacier-capped volcano made famous by Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach with its dramatic sea stacks and the ruins of a British trawler. Walk the Saxhóll crater rim if conditions permit.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back toward the Golden Circle (~2.5 hrs). Stop in Borgarnes for dinner at Settlement Center Restaurant before the final stretch. Return to guesthouse by 22:00.

meals.breakfast: Early guesthouse breakfast — pack snacks for the long day
meals.lunch: Bjargarsteinn Mathús in Grundarfjörður — fresh seafood overlooking the harbor with Kirkjufell in the background, ~3,000–4,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Settlement Center Restaurant, Borgarnes — excellent lamb and fish dishes with Viking-age themed décor, ~4,000–6,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (~5–6 hrs total driving). Start early to maximize the 5 hours of daylight. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is often called 'Iceland in miniature' — it packs glaciers, lava fields, fishing villages, and sea cliffs into one compact area.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning in the Golden Circle area — revisit your favorite spots from the trip for last photos and reflections. A slow morning walk around Þingvellir's Almannagjá gorge in the early winter light (~11:00) is magical for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Fontana Geothermal Baths in Laugarvatn one final time for a farewell soak — or try the nearby Laugarvatn village swimming pool (local community pool with hot tubs, ~800 ISK) for an authentic Icelandic 'sundlaug' experience. Pack bags and prepare for departure day.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep (if a third booking is available and conditions are favorable) — make the most of your last full night in Iceland's dark skies. Alternatively, enjoy a special farewell dinner and independent aurora watch.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final guesthouse breakfast — savor the skyr and Icelandic bread one last time
meals.lunch: Laugarvatn Fontana Café — geothermal rye bread and smoked trout for a fitting farewell lunch
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at Lindin Restaurant, Laugarvatn — splurge on the full tasting menu with Icelandic wine pairing; ~10,000–14,000 ISK per person for a memorable final evening

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight and prepare all documents for tomorrow's departure. Return any rental equipment. Set two alarms for an early departure. Leave a review for your boutique guesthouse if you enjoyed your stay.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of the boutique guesthouse. Drive to Keflavík International Airport (~1.5 hrs from Golden Circle hub). Depart early enough to allow for winter road conditions and airport check-in time (recommend 3 hours before flight). Return rental car at the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport departure — browse the duty-free for Icelandic souvenirs: Brennivín aquavit, Nói Síríus chocolate, Icelandic sea salt, lava salt, and lopapeysa wool sweaters. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in Iceland.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry memories of aurora-lit skies, steaming hot springs, volcanic landscapes, and the unique magic of Iceland in winter.

meals.breakfast: Early guesthouse breakfast before checkout, or grab pastries and coffee at a petrol station en route (N1 stations have decent food)
meals.lunch: Keflavík Airport restaurants — Fljúgur Café or Stofan for a final Icelandic lamb soup or smoked salmon bagel, ~2,500–3,500 ISK
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at layover airport

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for the airport drive in January — winter storms can cause delays on Route 41. Check road.is before departing. Keflavík Airport has good duty-free shopping with competitive prices on Icelandic products. The Blue Lagoon is located near the airport and opens at 07:00 — a pre-flight soak is possible if your flight departs after 12:00 and you book in advance (~9,990 ISK for the Comfort package).

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while waiting for the show.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal pool rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, a silica mud mask ritual, and a swim-up bar serving Icelandic craft beer. The surreal lava field backdrop makes it a bucket-list hot spring experience.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Morning (to avoid crowds) or Evening (for northern lights potential in season)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and steaming vents. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a glimpse into traditional Icelandic bathing culture in a stunning rural setting.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and cultural landmarks on a guided walking tour. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, and Icelandic hot dogs. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church, the colorful old harbor, and local artisan shops.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's breathtaking rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a natural geothermal hot spring soak at the end. The hike winds through obsidian lava fields, steaming fumaroles, and vivid mineral-streaked hillsides — one of Iceland's most dramatic landscapes.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavik International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to whisk you from the terminal in a heated premium vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Keflavik Airport to your boutique accommodation in the Golden Circle & Þingvellir area (approx. 1.5–2 hrs). En route, stop briefly at the dramatic lava fields of Nesjavellir for a first taste of Iceland's raw volcanic landscape. Check in, unpack, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — your guide picks you up from the hotel for a small-group jeep excursion into the dark Icelandic wilderness. January offers prime aurora-hunting conditions with up to 18 hours of darkness. Wrap up in provided thermal suits and enjoy hot cocoa under the stars.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge meal prior to landing
meals.lunch: Light welcome refreshments and Icelandic pastries prepared by your boutique hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friðheimar, a renowned tomato greenhouse restaurant near Reykholt serving farm-fresh tomato soup, bread, and seasonal Icelandic dishes in a magical glasshouse setting — reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: January darkness is your greatest ally for northern lights viewing. Keep aurora alert apps active throughout your stay. Ensure thermal layers and waterproof boots are accessible from your luggage immediately upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late-morning start with a gourmet Icelandic breakfast at the hotel. Then embark on a private guided tour of Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the Almannagjá gorge and learn about Iceland's ancient Viking parliament, the Alþingi, founded in 930 AD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the classic Golden Circle route with a private guide to the Haukadalur Geothermal Valley. Witness the mighty Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–40 metres into the winter sky. Explore the surrounding hot spring field and geothermal vents.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the majestic Gullfoss waterfall — the 'Golden Falls' — for a dramatic dusk viewing. The frozen mist and ice formations in January create an otherworldly spectacle. Return to the hotel for a warm-up before a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic gourmet breakfast at the boutique hotel — skyr, smoked lamb, fresh-baked rye bread, local cheeses, and organic eggs
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic hamper prepared by the hotel, enjoyed in a heated jeep at Haukadalur — smoked salmon open sandwiches, Icelandic cheese, and thermos of lamb soup
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn — an award-winning fine dining experience featuring locally sourced Icelandic ingredients including Arctic char, lamb, and foraged herbs, set beside the tranquil lake

day_by_day.notes: Dress in multiple thermal layers for outdoor sightseeing. Gullfoss can be icy underfoot — microspikes provided by your guide are recommended. The Golden Circle loop is approximately 300 km and best done with a private driver in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating to 1891. Soak in the naturally heated mineral-rich waters surrounded by steaming geothermal vents and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. In January, the steam rising against the dark sky is ethereal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Flúðir and visit a local greenhouse operation. Afternoon drive through the scenic Hvítá river valley. Optional snowshoe walk through snow-dusted lava fields with a local nature guide — a serene and exclusive experience arranged through the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a private in-room couples' or solo thermal bath experience if available at your boutique property. Followed by a curated tasting menu dinner at the hotel or a short drive to a premium local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet hotel breakfast featuring warm oatmeal porridge with Icelandic honey, skyr parfait, and freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at Kaffi Miðgarður in Flúðir — a cozy local café serving hearty lamb soup, fresh fish of the day, and homemade cakes
meals.dinner: Chef's tasting menu at your boutique hotel's private dining experience or at Reykholt's Húsið Restaurant — six-course seasonal Icelandic tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the Secret Lagoon in advance as January sees high demand. Arrive early morning to enjoy the lagoon with fewer visitors before tour buses arrive. Water temperature is a consistent 38–40°C — perfect for a cold winter morning.

day_by_day.morning: Private snowmobile or super-jeep excursion onto Langjökull glacier — Iceland's second-largest ice cap located just north of the Golden Circle. Explore the dramatic frozen landscape with an expert guide. Optional entry into the man-made ice tunnel inside the glacier for a truly unique underground experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Deildartunguhver, Europe's most powerful hot spring, pumping out 180 litres of boiling water per second. Nearby, stop at Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls — two of Iceland's most photogenic cascades where water bubbles up through ancient lava fields and tumbles into turquoise channels.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — a second dedicated aurora hunting evening. January skies offer excellent aurora probability. Your expert guide will drive to the darkest, clearest locations in the region based on real-time cloud forecasts.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast to prepare for the glacier excursion — smoked salmon bagels, boiled eggs, fresh fruit, and strong Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Warm lunch at Krauma Geothermal Baths & Restaurant near Deildartunguhver — freshly made lamb stew, fish soup, and locally baked bread in a beautifully designed lodge
meals.dinner: Dinner at Gamla Kaupfélagið in Borgarnes — a stylishly renovated historic co-op building serving premium Icelandic cuisine including reindeer, langoustine, and volcanic salt-cured fish

day_by_day.notes: Glacier excursions require sturdy waterproof boots and full thermal layers. The hotel can arrange all equipment rental. Langjökull is approximately 1.5 hours from the Golden Circle base — confirm departure time the evening before with your private guide.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic morning drive along Route 1 toward the South Coast. Stop at Seljalandsfoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most dramatic falls where a path leads behind the curtain of water (may be icy/closed in deep winter — your guide will confirm access). Continue to Skógafoss, a thundering 62-metre waterfall with a legendary treasure hidden behind it.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the black sand beach of Reynisfjara near Vík — one of the world's most striking beaches with towering basalt columns, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and powerful Atlantic waves. Strict safety protocols apply; your guide will brief you thoroughly. Continue to the nearby Dyrhólaey promontory for panoramic coastal views.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a premium South Coast property or return toward the Golden Circle base. Enjoy a refined dinner celebrating the dramatic landscapes of the day.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure — full Icelandic spread with hot and cold options
meals.lunch: Lunch at Skál! in Vík — a stylish eatery offering fresh fish tacos, lamb burgers, and Icelandic seafood chowder with panoramic views toward the black beach
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hótel Rangá's gourmet restaurant — one of Iceland's premier fine dining destinations, serving a seasonal menu of Icelandic lamb, Arctic char, and foie gras, with an in-house aurora alert system for guests

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach is beautiful but dangerous due to sneaker waves — never turn your back on the ocean and always follow your guide's instructions. January daylight is limited to approximately 5–6 hours, so timing is crucial to see all sites in natural light.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier hike on Sólheimajökull — a stunning outlet glacier of the Mýrdalsjökull ice cap. Strap on crampons and explore ice caves, crevasses, and dramatic blue ice formations with a certified glacier guide. This is one of Iceland's most accessible and visually spectacular glacier experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (long drive east, approximately 2.5 hours, best done as a dedicated day trip or combined with overnight). Alternatively, explore the Katla volcanic region and the hidden Kvernufoss waterfall — a secluded cascade near Skógafoss reached via a short hike, far fewer visitors than its famous neighbour.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward your Golden Circle base or overnight at a South Coast luxury property. Aurora watching from the hotel grounds if skies clear — the South Coast offers excellent dark sky conditions.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast at Hótel Rangá or your overnight property — eggs, bacon, smoked fish, skyr, and fresh bread
meals.lunch: Lunch at Suður-Vík Restaurant in Vík — known for its lamb soup, fish of the day, and homemade cakes with views of Reynisfjara
meals.dinner: Private in-hotel dining experience at Hótel Rangá with a customised chef's menu and optional Icelandic whisky or schnapps tasting

day_by_day.notes: Glacier hiking requires a minimum level of fitness and appropriate footwear — crampons and helmets are provided by the tour operator. Sólheimajökull is retreating due to climate change, making this a historically significant experience. Book certified glacier guides only.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — Iceland's deepest lake filled with magnificent icebergs calving from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier. In January, the lagoon is dramatically atmospheric with ice formations and occasional seals. Walk to Diamond Beach where crystal-clear ice chunks wash ashore on black sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding Vatnajökull National Park area. Visit Fjallsárlón lagoon — a quieter, equally beautiful glacial lagoon nearby. Optional private boat or zodiac tour on Jökulsárlón if ice conditions permit in January (confirm with operator). Drive back westward toward your base, stopping at scenic viewpoints along the Ring Road.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — third dedicated aurora evening. The remote South Coast and Highland edges offer some of Iceland's darkest skies. Your guide will position the group at optimal viewing locations.

meals.breakfast: Packed premium breakfast hamper from the hotel for the early long-distance drive — thermos of coffee, smoked salmon wraps, fruit, and pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at Jökulsárlón Café (Glacier Lagoon Café) — hearty lamb soup, lobster bisque, and freshly baked bread in a warm, rustic setting overlooking the lagoon
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hótel Skaftafell or Fosshotel Glacier Lagoon's restaurant — locally inspired menu featuring slow-roasted lamb, reindeer, and glacial water-poached Arctic char

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón is approximately 4–4.5 hours from the Golden Circle — this is a long driving day. Consider an overnight stay at Fosshotel Glacier Lagoon (luxury property) to reduce driving and maximise lagoon time at different light conditions. Confirm with your travel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Return journey toward Reykjavik with a scenic stop at Þórsmörk Nature Reserve (accessible by super-jeep in winter). This hidden highland valley surrounded by three glaciers offers dramatic winter scenery and exclusive access in January when most tourists are absent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Reykjavik by early afternoon. Check into a luxury Reykjavik city hotel (e.g., The Reykjavik EDITION or Hotel Borg) for a mid-trip urban interlude. Freshen up and take a private walking orientation of the city — Hallgrímskirkja church, Harpa Concert Hall, and the Old Harbour.
day_by_day.evening: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour — explore the capital's vibrant culinary scene with a knowledgeable local guide. Sample traditional Icelandic delicacies including hákarl (fermented shark), skyr desserts, langoustine, and craft Icelandic spirits at curated stops across the city.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your overnight South Coast property before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Matur og Drykkur in Reykjavik — a celebrated restaurant dedicated to traditional Icelandic recipes reimagined with modern technique, featuring cod cheeks, lamb head, and rye bread ice cream
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dill Restaurant — Iceland's first and only Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a stunning New Nordic tasting menu with Icelandic ingredients, natural wines, and impeccable service. Advance booking essential.

day_by_day.notes: Dill Restaurant requires reservations weeks or months in advance — ensure your travel concierge books this before departure from home. The Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour is best experienced on an empty stomach — plan accordingly and skip heavy afternoon snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Private cultural tour of Reykjavik's top museums — begin at the National Museum of Iceland for a deep dive into Viking history and Icelandic heritage. Continue to the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) built around actual Viking Age ruins discovered beneath the city streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — the crown jewel of Icelandic spa experiences. Book the premium Retreat Spa package for exclusive access to the private lagoon, in-water massage treatments, silica mud masks, algae masks, and a gourmet in-water dining experience. The milky-blue 38–40°C waters surrounded by black lava in January are absolutely magical.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik for a leisurely evening. Explore the Laugavegur shopping street for premium Icelandic design, wool goods, and artisan gifts. Enjoy a cocktail at the rooftop bar of your luxury hotel before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet hotel breakfast at your Reykjavik luxury property — extensive buffet with Icelandic specialities, fresh juices, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: In-water dining at the Blue Lagoon's LAVA Restaurant — enjoy langoustine, sushi, and Icelandic seafood while floating in the geothermal waters with a glass of Cava
meals.dinner: Dinner at Grillið Restaurant atop the Radisson Blu Saga Hotel — Reykjavik's premier rooftop fine dining with panoramic city and mountain views, serving premium Icelandic lamb, seafood, and seasonal tasting menus

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa packages must be booked well in advance — the Retreat is a separate, more exclusive section of the lagoon with limited capacity. Remove all jewellery before entering as silica-rich water can discolour metals. Hair conditioning treatment is recommended before soaking.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour departing from Reykjavik — soar over the Golden Circle, Þingvellir National Park, and active geothermal areas from above. In January, snow-covered volcanic landscapes from the air are breathtaking. Optional landing on a remote glacier or highland plateau for a champagne toast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to your Golden Circle boutique accommodation. Afternoon at leisure — enjoy the hotel's private facilities, take a soak in any on-site hot tub or geothermal pool, and rest after the excitement of the city days.
day_by_day.evening: Private stargazing and aurora watching session arranged through the hotel — a local astronomer guide accompanies you to a dark sky location with telescopes and aurora monitoring equipment. Hot chocolate and Icelandic spirits provided.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Reykjavik before checkout and helicopter departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic prepared by the helicopter tour operator — enjoyed at a remote highland landing spot with champagne and premium Icelandic snacks
meals.dinner: Intimate private chef dinner at your Golden Circle boutique hotel — a bespoke menu designed around your preferences using local lamb, fish, and seasonal produce, served in your suite or private dining room

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours are weather-dependent and may be rescheduled — have a backup plan (e.g., a super-jeep highland tour) ready. Confirm helicopter availability and weight limits when booking. The private chef dinner should be arranged 48 hours in advance with the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike — a super-jeep expedition into the Highland interior to reach Iceland's most colourful landscape. Trek through rainbow-coloured rhyolite mountains streaked in red, orange, green, and purple, passing obsidian lava fields and steaming fumaroles. This is a bucket-list Icelandic experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the Landmannalaugar hot spring pool — a natural geothermal river where hot spring water mixes with a cold stream creating the perfect bathing temperature. Soak in this wild, remote hot spring surrounded by dramatic highland scenery. Return journey through the highland interior by super-jeep.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — fourth aurora opportunity. After the physical exertion of the day, wrap up in thermal gear and let your guide take you to the best aurora viewing spots. The highland region offers exceptional dark skies.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty hotel breakfast — oatmeal, eggs, smoked meats, and strong coffee to fuel the highland hike
meals.lunch: Packed premium highland picnic provided by your super-jeep tour operator — thermos of lamb soup, open-faced sandwiches, Icelandic chocolate, and hot drinks enjoyed at Landmannalaugar
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn (revisit for a different seasonal menu) or at Efstidalur II Farm Restaurant — a working dairy farm restaurant serving farm-to-table meals including homemade ice cream, fresh beef, and dairy dishes

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar is only accessible by 4WD super-jeep in winter — standard vehicles cannot reach it. The hike is moderate difficulty and requires waterproof hiking boots, thermal layers, and a swimsuit for the hot spring. The route may be adjusted based on weather and road conditions on the day.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at your boutique hotel. Enjoy a long breakfast, spa treatment if available, or a gentle walk around the Þingvellir lakeshore (Þingvallavatn — Iceland's largest natural lake). The peaceful winter morning atmosphere and potential frost on the landscape is utterly serene.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided snorkelling or diving experience in Silfra fissure at Þingvellir National Park — one of the world's top dive sites where you float between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility exceeding 100 metres. Dry suits are provided. An extraordinary once-in-a-lifetime experience.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell aurora evening — a final Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep with your guide. Celebrate the journey with a thermos of Brennivín (Icelandic aquavit) under the dancing green lights of the aurora borealis. A perfect penultimate evening.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full gourmet hotel breakfast — take your time and savour every element of the Icelandic spread
meals.lunch: Lunch at Þingvellir National Park Visitor Centre Café — fish soup, open sandwiches, and Icelandic pastries with views over the rift valley
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at your boutique hotel — arrange in advance for a private dining experience with a curated six-course menu, Icelandic wine and spirit pairing, and personalised service celebrating your 13-day journey

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkelling/diving requires advance booking and a medical fitness declaration. Water temperature is 2–4°C year-round — dry suits keep you warm and no swimming ability is required for snorkelling. This is a non-negotiable bucket-list experience if you are comfortable in water. Minimum age and health requirements apply.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Take a last walk around the Golden Circle area, breathe in the crisp Icelandic air, and savour the silence of the volcanic landscape. Pack and prepare for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from the Golden Circle to Keflavik International Airport (approximately 1.5–2 hours). En route, stop for a final soak at the Sky Lagoon in Reykjavik — a premium geothermal spa with an infinity edge pool overlooking the North Atlantic Ocean, a seven-step ritual including sauna, cold plunge, steam room, and mist room. A perfect send-off.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Keflavik International Airport. Carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days — auroras, glaciers, geothermal wonders, and the wild magic of Iceland.

meals.breakfast: Final Icelandic hotel breakfast — request any favourite items from the week to be prepared specially as a farewell meal
meals.lunch: Sky Lagoon's Gelmir Lagoon Bar — enjoy Icelandic seafood bites, smoked salmon, and a glass of sparkling wine while floating in the infinity pool overlooking the Atlantic
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining at Keflavik or an early dinner at Perlan (The Pearl) in Reykjavik — a glass-domed landmark restaurant with 360-degree panoramic views over the capital and surrounding mountains, serving premium Icelandic seafood and lamb

day_by_day.notes: Sky Lagoon requires advance booking — the Sér (Pure) package includes the seven-step ritual and is the premium option. Allow at least 2–2.5 hours at the lagoon plus travel time to the airport. Arrive at Keflavik at least 2.5 hours before international departure. Duty-free Icelandic spirits, chocolates, and skincare products make excellent final purchases at the airport.
